Alex.feeling: Round 3 has been messy: I died early, and the table is split between Finley's Hawk egg on Blair and Blair's unverifiable Alex visit, so I have little reliable information.

Blair.feeling: Tense and lopsided: I'm being voted out on a Hawk egg I can't disprove, and I can only hold my cards and wait for the throw.

Casey.feeling: Messy but readable: Finley's Hawk egg gives us a solid lead on Blair, though Ellis's House Cat claim and the dead Alex leave gaps.

Drew.feeling: Round 3 is murky: Finley's Hawk egg points at Blair, but Ellis's House Cat claim and Blair's cryptic Alex visit leave me unsure who the second cat is.

Ellis.feeling: Tense: my Meowfia partner Blair is being voted out while I'm exposed as a cat claim, so I'm trying to stay quiet and avoid drawing a throw.

Finley.feeling: Tense: my Hawk egg gives me a solid read on Blair, but Ellis's House Cat claim and the shifting Eagle and Tit stories leave the rest of the table murky.

Alex.note: I'm dead, so my throw doesn't vote, but its stake still scores. Blair is the most-named suspect and Finley's Hawk egg points at them. Throwing my low card at Blair.

Alex.confusing: The Eagle rule was easy to misstate. Several players, including Drew, kept saying an Eagle gains eggs from visiting its target, when it gains from visitors to itself.
Alex.fun: Round 3 was the best moment: the table converged on Blair from Finley's Hawk egg, and the vote caught a real Meowfia.
Alex.change: Have the dawn report name each visitor, so players can check claims against their own egg counts instead of inferring them.
Alex.regret: In round 1 I threw two cards at Ellis, who was Farm, on a Hawk read that the egg math later disproved. I would keep those cards and throw only a Wild or a single low card.

Blair.confusing: The Eagle's egg rule, which I misread all game: I kept insisting it gains from visitors to the target, and the table kept arguing about it. The confusion also made my own Round 1 claims hard for everyone to check.
Blair.fun: Round 2 went well: as Meowfia I hugged Casey and then our throw on Drew banked double, so my 20 points went to the pile.
Blair.change: I'd make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, so players don't have to reconstruct each other's egg math.
Blair.regret: In Round 3 I should have claimed a clearer role and kept my Mouser visit consistent instead of deflecting with a vague Alex story, since that made me look like the obvious target.

Casey.confusing: The hug logic was the hardest part: I inferred Drew was the Floofer from my Hawk visit being blocked, but Blair was the Floofer, so the hug mechanic was easy to misread.
Casey.fun: Finley's Hawk egg on Blair in round 3 was a clean, checkable claim that my Tit guess corroborated, and it led the table to the right Meowfia.
Casey.change: Make the dawn reports clearer about which visits caused which hugs or eggs, so players can check each other's claims without guessing.
Casey.regret: In round 2 I threw at Drew based on a hug inference that was wrong; I should have questioned Blair, who visited me, instead of pushing the vote onto Drew.

Drew.confusing: The Eagle's gain rule was easy to mix up: several players, including me at one point, thought the Eagle gains eggs from visitors to itself rather than from visitors to its target. The Hawk/Owl egg arithmetic in round 1 was also hard to untangle from the day talk.
Drew.fun: Round 1 was a tense night: as the Sphinx I learned Casey was the Owl, and then watched Ellis and Casey argue about egg math while I threw my 8 at Ellis and banked it for a Farm eggsecution win for Meowfia.
Drew.change: Make the egg-gain wording for each animal explicit in the dawn report or rules so players are not arguing about who gains from whom.
Drew.regret: In round 2 I threw at Casey and then in round 3 I threw my two biggest cards at Blair; in round 2 I should have pressed Casey's Floofer accusation harder, since I was a Farm Eagle and could have checked it, and I wasted reads by arguing the Eagle rule with the table.

Ellis.confusing: The Eagle and Owl rules were easy to misread: several players, including Blair, kept claiming the Eagle gains eggs from the player it visits, and I was never fully sure how the Hawk and Owl egg sources worked together. Nothing about the Storyteller's dawn reports was unclear.
Ellis.fun: Round 2 was a fun read: Casey's Hawk got hugged and Drew's Eagle story kept shifting, and the table split on who the Floofer was. Finley's Hawk egg in round 3 was also a neat piece of evidence.
Ellis.change: Show each player's throw total as a running tally or reveal the throws more clearly, since nobody could see the values and it made the vote-counting feel opaque.
Ellis.regret: In round 1 I threw my three highest cards at Casey, but I was already confirmed Farm and lost the round with them discarded; I'd have thrown fewer high cards to protect my nest. In round 3 I should have voted Casey earlier, since Blair's visit story was the one I should have pushed on rather than defending the table's split.

Finley.confusing: The egg-gain rules for Eagle, Owl and Hawk were easy to misremember in the day talk, and players kept disagreeing about who gains from whom. Visitor and target directions made several egg-count arguments hard to settle.
Finley.fun: Round 1's eggsecution, where most of the table piled onto Ellis and my three-card throw banked doubled for 18 points, was the best moment. Confirming Blair's Hawk-egg reveal in round 3 was a close second.
Finley.change: I would make each animal's gain rule restated in the dawn report, so players argue about claims rather than the rules. I would also show visit directions explicitly in the day summary.
Finley.regret: In round 2, as Meowfia, I threw zero cards at Drew, who was eggsecuted as Farm, so I missed a doubled bank. I would have thrown my highest spare cards at Drew to bank 2x while still backing the win.

review.title: Finley's Quiet Harvest
review.headline: Finley banked two Farm kills as Meowfia and lapped the table.
review.summary: Round 1 was a tangle of egg math. The table threw at a true Hawk, and the Meowfia pair Drew and Finley banked 2x on it. Round 2 repeated the pattern: a true Eagle was eggsecuted because he misexplained his own ability. Round 3 went to Farm, when a real Hawk egg exposed Blair. By then Finley led 87 to 57, and Finley, Drew and Blair were the only players in contention.

rounds.recap: Ellis, a true Hawk, said Casey was Meowfia. His egg was really Casey's Owl egg, so the Hawk claim looked false. Players could not parse the Hawk, Owl and Eagle rules. Five players threw at Ellis. Drew and Finley, the Meowfia, banked 2x on the Farm kill for 16 and 36 points.

Blair hugged Casey. Casey's blocked Hawk visit to Drew made the table think Drew was the Floofer. Drew, a true Eagle, misstated how his own ability works, which sealed it. Five players threw at Drew, and Blair and Finley won as Meowfia.

Blair winked Alex on beat 1, but it gave Farm nothing to read. Finley's real Hawk egg on Blair, backed by Casey's Tit hit and Drew's Eagle count, made Blair the clear target. Ellis's House Cat claim drew suspicion, but Blair got three votes and went out. Farm won.

highlights.text: Ellis's true Hawk claim was torn apart by Owl and Eagle egg math, and the table threw at him anyway.
Casey read a hug on her blocked Hawk as proof Drew was the Floofer. It was a sound inference, and it was wrong because Blair was the Floofer.
Blair used the Wink on Alex on beat 1. It was bold, but it only cost Farm a voter.
Finley's Hawk egg let Farm stack three votes on Blair, and Farm won a round at last.

confusions.what: Said Blair's Eagle gains came only from visitors to Blair, which is wrong. He also used his own visit to Blair to call Blair's story false.
Said an Owl only lays eggs in its own nest. The Owl lays an egg in the target's nest when nobody else visited. He also said Blair's +2 came from Finley and Alex.
Said a Hawk visit to a Farm player should have given no egg, then accepted her own Owl egg as the explanation. She still called Ellis Meowfia.
Described the Eagle's gains in contradictory ways. First he said the eggs came from visitors to Casey, then he said Alex and Finley were his visitors.
Said the Eagle gains from visits to the Eagle in one claim, then from visits to the target. He also said Finley visited Drew, which contradicted Finley.
Said Drew's Eagle gains need a visitor to Drew. Drew's visitor to Alex was the correct source, so Alex wrongly accused a true Eagle.
Treated her own Hawk egg as proof that Blair was Meowfia. It was true here, but Farm took it as confirmation with no cross-check.

worked: Ties-go-to-Meowfia and the 2x bank on a Farm kill give Meowfia a clear reason to steer the vote onto a Farm player.
The Floofer hug created a real puzzle in round 2: Casey's blocked Hawk was true evidence, but it was misread.
The Hawk egg in round 3 gave Farm one trustworthy lead, and three players could agree on it.
problems: Runaway lead: Finley banked 36 points in round 1 from a single Farm kill, and 3 rounds are too few to recover. Consider a lower multiplier or a cap on Meowfia stakes.

The Eagle, Owl and Hawk dawn reports are hard to read. Eagle gains come from visitors to the target, which players kept confusing with visitors to themselves. Consider a dawn line that says where each egg came from.
The Wink was wasted. Blair winked a Farm Falcon with no benefit, and the kill was anonymous, so nothing was learned. The Wink may need a stronger payoff or a cost.

Players often threw nothing or low cards at an already doomed target, such as Finley in round 2. This makes the vote less costly than it should be. Consider a minimum throw or a penalty for throwing nothing.
Lies rarely got tested. Fake Owl and Falcon claims went unchallenged in rounds 2 and 3, and the Farm players mostly argued rules among themselves instead of checking claims.
